This is a seller-FAQ topic page, not an area page: titled "FAQ for Home Sellers in BC | Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®," it is built as five themed answer sections — Pricing & Timing; Marketing & Showings; Offers & Negotiation; Preparing Your Home; Costs & Logistics — followed by a structured eight-question FAQ block and a home-evaluation call to action, for BC sellers generally with Fraser Valley and Greater Vancouver framing throughout.

items.t: The page's structure as read: five themed sections (Pricing & Timing; Marketing & Showings; Offers & Negotiation; Preparing Your Home; Costs & Logistics), then a structured eight-question FAQ block (Why isn't my home selling?; Should I sell before buying?; Should I price high and lower later?; Do I need a REALTOR?; What are the costs of selling?; Will renovations increase value?; When is the best time to sell?; Do I have to accept an offer?), a "See What's Selling in Your Neighbourhood" search block, and a complimentary market evaluation call to action. The structured FAQ's eight answers substantially repeat the themed sections above them on the same page — a rebuild consideration, recorded as read.

Where condo stock concentrates for this page: nowhere geographic — the page names no neighbourhood, building or complex, and its "stock" is any BC home a seller is deciding whether and how to list, condos included only as one home type among others.

items.t: The regulator frame (BCFSA) — the verified frame behind this page's answers: a licensed real estate professional must give consumers information about commissions and fees, inform consumers of the duties and responsibilities owed to clients and non-clients, inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party, and only work for either the buyer or the seller in a transaction; the representation, duties and BCFSA complaint-route disclosures must happen at the outset of dealings.

Selling without a licence, verified at the regulator: a person does not require a licence to provide real estate services to themselves — for example, by selling or renting out their own property — while a person must not provide real estate services to or on behalf of another, for or in expectation of remuneration, unless licensed or exempt. That supports the page's "not legally required to use a REALTOR®" answer.

Property transfer tax is the buyer's tax: PTT is payable by the purchaser on the fair market value of the property on the day it is registered at the Land Title Office — the page's repeated statement, "property transfer tax is paid by the buyer, not the seller," matches that frame. General rates: 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million, 3% above $2 million, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3 million. Newly Built Home Exemption: full to $1,100,000, partial to $1,150,000.

GST and rebates (seller-relevant edge): 5% GST applies to new construction, not resales — a resale condo seller does not charge GST. First-Time Home Buyers' GST/HST Rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122) — 100% of GST to $1M, maximum $50,000, phasing to $1.5M, agreements March 20, 2025–2031; GST New Housing Rebate 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350,000–$450,000 phase-out.

Page claims recorded as page statements only — not verified: the seasonality pattern (November through January slowest, spring pick-up by March, softer August, September rebound); standard completion timelines of 45–60 days from accepted offer (and 2 weeks to 9 months in the structured FAQ) and the bridge-financing description (firm accepted offers on both sides required; setup fee and daily interest); the claim that a seller "may be required to accept" a cash offer at list price matching listed "cash" terms, with "set your terms as TBD" advice; listing contracts typically 4–6 months with a claimed 60-day minimum under the named board's rules; and the BC PST on real estate services point in the article linked from Costs & Logistics. No official, board or lender source for any of these was opened pass.

The regulator's consumer framework — BCFSA: a licensed professional must give consumers information about commissions and fees, inform consumers of the duties and responsibilities owed to clients and non-clients, inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party, and only work for either the buyer or the seller in a transaction; the representation, duties and complaint-route disclosures must happen at the outset of dealings. The page states no commission rate or amount.

PTT is the buyer's tax — Province: PTT is payable by the purchaser on the fair market value of the property on the day it is registered at the Land Title Office; the page's repeated statement that "property transfer tax is paid by the buyer, not the seller" matches that frame.

: where a buyer rescinds under the Home Buyer Rescission Period Regulation within three business days, the brokerage pays the seller the 0.25% rescission fee directly and returns the remaining deposit balance to the buyer, with no separate release form; otherwise a deposit is held in the brokerage's trust account with the brokerage as stakeholder, and is not automatically returned if subjects are not removed. Strata block (a seller of a bare-land strata lot): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for 5+ lots since Jul 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF since Nov 1, 2023; rental bylaws VOID since Nov 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions).

GST on vacant land — CRA GI-003 level only (for a seller of land): developer/business sales and newly subdivided lots generally TAXABLE; an individual's sale of personal-use land generally exempt. Finer points not confirmed.

faq.q: Why isn't my home selling, per the page?
faq.a: The page's answer, as a page statement: generally for one or more of three reasons — it is overpriced relative to comparable recent sales and current competition, it is not marketed well enough online and offline, or it does not show well; the fix starts with a home evaluation and an honest comparison against recent sales, active listings and expired or terminated listings.

faq.q: What are the costs of selling a home in BC, per the page?
faq.a: The page lists real estate commission (split between the listing agent and the buyer's agent), cleaning, staging and preparation, legal fees and disbursements, and a possible mortgage penalty if the mortgage is broken early — and states no commission figure, which BCFSA's framework places in the listing conversation, where a licensee must give consumers information about commissions and fees.

faq.q: Do I have to accept an offer on my home?
faq.a: The page's answer, as a page statement: no — on receiving an offer you can accept it as-is, counter, or reject it altogether; a counter voids the previous offer.

faq.q: Who pays the property transfer tax when I sell?
faq.a: The buyer: PTT is payable by the purchaser on the fair market value of the property on the day it is registered at the Land Title Office — when you buy your next home, you pay it as the buyer.

faq.q: Should I price high and lower later?
faq.a: The page's answer, carried as a page statement: no — pricing high and reducing later fails because the first two weeks on market are critical and a reduced listing reads as stale.

faq.q: Will renovations increase my sale price by what they cost?
